rule: module = the `module` header (else the file name); top-level functions, class methods and record fields `Module.f` Bare names resolve through local bindings, the module, import lists (with `T (..)` fields and hiding), unqualified imports of scanned modules (following `module M` re-exports and export lists), the Prelude (`Prelude.show`, medium) and the one unlisted external import; qualified imports `Map.size` medium. **C7 Complete edges.** Caller and callee are never empty. The line is the line of the callee's name, per the ID-format rules.
source: KNOWN_GAP: backtick-infix calls (x `f` y) are almost never emitted
notes: `x `f` y` is the application `f x y` of the named function f written infix; it calls f, which resolves like any bare name: `Infix.combine` (module, high), `Prelude.div` (Prelude, medium). `nested` applies `combine` twice (two edges on one line) and `halve` once. This is not an operator symbol application, so it does not depend on the operator spec_gap (case 16).
